events.content: Equinix Q2 2026 earnings release revenue AI leasing xScale

**Q1 2026 revenue:** Equinix reported revenue of **$2.444 billion** for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, up **10% year over year** as reported and **8%** on a normalized, constant-currency basis. [[1]]

**AI demand / leasing:** The company delivered **$378 million of annualized gross bookings** and roughly **$140 million of annualized presales**—a record presales level—with approximately **60% of its largest deals AI-related**. [[1]]

**xScale timing:** Q1 revenue and results **did not include the Hampton xScale lease transaction**; Equinix said that, excluding the timing effect of that deal, Q1 performance was above the midpoint of its Q1 revenue-guidance range. [[1]]

**Read-through:** The deferred xScale lease is a timing issue rather than evidence of weak underlying demand, as management indicated it was negotiating expanded mutually beneficial terms and expected the associated economics to be reflected in Q2 guidance. [[2]]

**Important nuance:** Equinix did not disclose a stand-alone dollar amount for “AI leasing” revenue in Q1; the clearest disclosed AI indicators are the AI mix of large deals, the record bookings/presales, and the postponed Hampton xScale transaction. [[1]]

events.content: Equinix Q1 2026 earnings call AI-related leasing demand xScale annualized bookings

**Q2 2026 takeaway:** Equinix characterized demand as broad-based and stronger than its prior long-term planning assumptions, with demand split between large enterprises modernizing legacy on-premises infrastructure and net-new AI-native workloads/service providers. [[1]]

- Equinix closed **134 MW of xScale leases** in Q2 2026, including the Hampton transaction, which generated roughly **$120 million of non-recurring fees**. [[1]]
- Management said **“the vast majority” of its largest Q2 deals were driven by AI workloads**, consistent with the prior several quarters. [[1]]
- Importantly, the company did **not** disclose that all 134 MW of xScale leasing was AI-specific; the more supportable reading is that AI is a major demand accelerant across its portfolio, while xScale leasing activity includes hyperscale capacity transactions such as Hampton. [[1]]
- The strength translated into a capacity-response plan: Equinix added nine projects since April and had **52 projects underway across 33 markets** at quarter-end. [[2]]
- Q2 revenue was **$2.625 billion**, up **16% year over year**, with growth aided by underlying execution and one-time xScale fees. [[3]]
- Management’s practical demand signal was raised outlook and an accelerated expansion program, with long-term annual capex envisioned at **$5 billion–$7 billion**, excluding real-estate acquisitions and xScale. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** The transcript supports a bullish AI-led leasing thesis—AI drove most large deals and is helping sustain capacity demand—but it does not support equating the full 134 MW of Q2 xScale leases directly to AI demand. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: Equinix FY 2025 annual revenue AI demand leasing

events.content: Equinix FY 2025 annual revenue AI demand leasing

Equinix generated FY2025 revenue of **$9.217 billion**, up **5% year over year as reported** and **6% on a normalized, constant-currency basis**, for the year ended December 31, 2025. [[1]] 

Its xScale hyperscale/AI platform had **more than 430 MW leased** across **23 operational facilities in 13 metros** at Q4 2025; Equinix also delivered **more than 90 MW of xScale capacity during 2025**. [[2]] [[3]] 

The reported xScale leasing figure is platform-wide leased power capacity rather than a separately disclosed FY2025 AI-only leasing subtotal. [[2]] [[4]]

Related coverage:
**Bottom line:** Federal Reserve tightening is generally a valuation headwind for data-center REITs, while easing is generally supportive, because policy-rate surprises have historically had economically meaningful negative effects on equity REIT prices; one study estimates an unexpected 25-basis-point Fed cut is associated with roughly a 2% rise in U.S. equity-REIT prices on average. [[1]]

**The primary valuation channel is the required return.** A data-center REIT’s enterprise value is commonly framed as stabilized property NOI divided by a cap rate, or as the present value of future cash flows discounted at a required return; higher risk-free rates and often wider credit/equity risk premiums raise those required returns, pushing values lower if NOI is unchanged. [[2]] [[1]]

**Cap-rate sensitivity is especially material because the sector begins from low yields.** Data-center REITs were reported at an implied cap rate of about 4.4% in 2025, the lowest among major REIT property sectors; holding NOI constant, a 50-basis-point move from 4.4% to 4.9% reduces the simple NOI/cap-rate value by about 10.2%. [[3]] [[4]]

**Rates also affect the cost and availability of growth capital.**

**Equinix – AI-driven leasing demand & revenue (most recent periods)**  

| Period | Revenue | Key AI / xScale leasing figure(s) | Source |
|--------|---------|-----------------------------------|--------|
| Q1 2026 (ended Mar 2026) | **$2.444 B** (↑10% YoY) | AI‑related large deals represented ~**60%** of the record $140 M annualized presales; **$378 M annualized gross bookings**. | S2.1 |
| Q2 2026 (ended Jun 2026) | **$2.625 B** (↑16% YoY) | Closed **134 MW of xScale leases** (including the Hampton transaction, ~$120 M non‑recurring fees); management said “the vast majority” of its largest Q2 deals were AI‑driven. | S3.1‑S3.3 |
| FY 2025 (ended Dec 2025) | **$9.217 B** (↑5% YoY) | xScale platform **> 430 MW leased** across **23 facilities in 13 metros** (platform‑wide capacity; not broken out as AI‑only). | S5.1‑S5.4 |

**Summary**

- **Revenue growth** has been steady: 10% YoY in Q1 2026, accelerating to 16% YoY in Q2 2026, and 5% for the full year 2025.  
- **AI demand** is the clearest leasing driver disclosed: roughly 60% of the largest deals in Q1 2026 were AI‑related, and management consistently flagged AI as a “major demand accelerant” in Q2 2026, with most large deals AI‑focused.  
- **xScale leasing** (Equinix’s hyperscale/AI capacity) reached **> 430 MW** by end‑2025 and **134 MW** were closed in Q2 2026 (including the one‑‑time Hampton fees). The company notes that while AI is a strong demand catalyst, not all xScale leases are exclusively AI‑driven.  

All figures are supported by cited sources (S2.1, S3.1‑S3.3, S5.1‑S5.4).

private_messages.content:
**Q2 2026 takeaway:** Equinix characterized demand as broad-based and stronger than its prior long-term planning assumptions, with demand split between large enterprises modernizing legacy on-premises infrastructure and net-new AI-native workloads/service providers. [[1]]

- Equinix closed **134 MW of xScale leases** in Q2 2026, including the Hampton transaction, which generated roughly **$120 million of non-recurring fees**. [[1]]
- Management said **“the vast majority” of its largest Q2 deals were driven by AI workloads**, consistent with the prior several quarters. [[1]]
- Importantly, the company did **not** disclose that all 134 MW of xScale leasing was AI-specific; the more supportable reading is that AI is a major demand accelerant across its portfolio, while xScale leasing activity includes hyperscale capacity transactions such as Hampton. [[1]]
- The strength translated into a capacity-response plan: Equinix added nine projects since April and had **52 projects underway across 33 markets** at quarter-end. [[2]]
- Q2 revenue was **$2.625 billion**, up **16% year over year**, with growth aided by underlying execution and one-time xScale fees. [[3]]
- Management’s practical demand signal was raised outlook and an accelerated expansion program, with long-term annual capex envisioned at **$5 billion–$7 billion**, excluding real-estate acquisitions and xScale. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** The transcript supports a bullish AI-led leasing thesis—AI drove most large deals and is helping sustain capacity demand—but it does not support equating the full 134 MW of Q2 xScale leases directly to AI demand. [[1]]
